Beregdaroc Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Szabadság út 99, Hungary

Not demolished. Beregdaróc's Jewish community existed as early as 1855, per its earliest found tombstone, though it is said to have persisted until 1944; the population numbered 56 among 850 residents in 1880, declining to 38 by 1930 before rising slightly to 48 (3.6 percent) by 1941. The small community, numbering between 30 and 100 people, gathered primarily for Sabbath services at a synagogue on Szabadság Street, now used as a private home. Following the German occupation, the Jews of Beregdaróc were confined in the Beregszász Ghetto; the final transport from there to Auschwitz departed May 29, 1944, one of about 40,000 Jews deported from Beregszász that month.
